title: A Wildfire Spun Up a Tornado of Fire With 143 mph Winds

scenes.text: A wildfire once spun up a tornado made of fire.
July 2018, Redding, California. Winds inside it hit more than 140 miles an hour.
It stood around 18,000 feet tall. Taller than any mountain in the lower forty-eight states.
Flames and debris inside it reached about 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit.
Only one other fire tornado like it has ever been documented. Canberra, 2003.

description:
A wildfire once spun up a tornado made of fire.
On 26 July 2018 the Carr Fire near Redding, California produced a fire vortex with winds above 140 miles an hour, estimated to stand about 18,000 feet tall. Only one other fire tornado has ever been documented, in Canberra in 2003.
Would you have run or filmed it? Tell us in the comments.
first_comment: The fire cloud above it rose to about 39,000 feet. Higher than most airliners fly. Would you stay or run?
